chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the ring when I perform the ritual bath (Ghusl). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Turn it around from its place.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'With regard to the ablution (Wudu), turn it around, and if you forget [to remove it] until you stand in the prayer, then I do not order you to repeat the prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wearing a ring during Wudu and Ghusl, and does forgetting to remove it invalidate the prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides specific juristic guidance on the etiquette of wearing a ring during purification, distinguishing between the thorough rotation required in Ghusl and the simpler turning in Wudu to ensure water reaches beneath it. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on the validity of acts despite minor oversights, as evidenced by the concession that forgetting to remove the ring does not invalidate the subsequent prayer. The narration reflects the practical application of ritual purity laws, ensuring that adornments do not hinder the completeness of the ablution.
